criteria_results.text: Day-column Add task opens the full inspector pre-seeded with that day; saving creates the task on that day (with the companion backend fix landed).
criteria_results.notes: User: 'Test task created on Weds showed weds scheduled date in the inspector but when I saved it, it got put into backlog and re-opening inspector revealed the scheduled date was not applied.' Client sent the field correctly (UI showed seeded date); production server dropped it because the Synology container is still running the pre-#674 image. The 'API Deploy (Synology)' GH workflow only PUBLISHES the image to GHCR — deployment (docker compose pull + up -d on the NAS) is manual per docs/release/hosted_deployment_synology_cloudflare.md and was never executed. Code on main is verified correct for both DB paths (postgres createAsync inserts scheduled_date at $5).

criteria_results.text: Verify on both DB paths if feasible (production Postgres + local SQLite).
criteria_results.notes: Postgres-path verification was correctly flagged UNVERIFIED in the contract; the smoke that was supposed to close it ran against a stale container, so it remains open until the NAS restarts on the new image.

process_issues.description: The GitHub workflow named 'API Deploy (Synology)' builds and publishes the image to GHCR but does NOT restart the Synology container — deployment is a documented manual step (ssh + docker compose pull + up -d). The workflow name invites the misreading that green run == deployed. There is also no way to verify the running server's code version remotely: /health returns only {status, service}, so a stale container is indistinguishable from a fresh one.
process_issues.detected_by: Reading .github/workflows/api_deploy_synology.yml (publish-only, final step echoes the manual pull command) and docs/release/hosted_deployment_synology_cloudflare.md ('Deployment is manual').

issues.description: After the publish workflow went green, the orchestrator told the user 'API deploy is live — the #674 scheduledDate fix is now on production' with only a /health 200 as evidence. /health does not identify the running code version; the claim was premature and sent the user into a smoke that was guaranteed to fail on the headline criterion. The runbook stating 'Deployment is manual' was in-repo and unread at claim time.
issues.detected_by: Transcript inspection: completion claim vs. runbook docs/release/hosted_deployment_synology_cloudflare.md.

failure_output: Task created from Wednesday day column with seeded scheduled date visible in inspector; after save, task appeared in backlog and re-opened inspector showed no scheduled date applied.
suggested_follow_up: Make deployments verifiable: expose the build commit/version in GET /health (and bake it into the image at build time) so 'new image is running' is a one-curl check, and either rename the publish workflow or add an automated/verified restart step.

resolution.action: User ran the runbook's routine update on the Synology (docker compose pull + up -d); container restarted on the new ghcr image. Re-smoke: planner task created on Wednesday landed in the Wednesday column with scheduled date persisted. Confirms C5 diagnosis (stale container) — no code change needed.
